title: How Bridgewater Turned 100 Million Documents Into an Edge - Sam Green & Aaron Linsky, Bridgewater
talk_summary: Bridgewater built a governed unstructured-data platform (the Vault) with 100M+ documents, tuned separately for human precision and agent scale, and used it to make agents proactive participants in research. The transferable lessons are about building a small hand-labeled retrieval benchmark, filtering-aware search, and capturing agent/human synthesis back into the corpus.

takeaways.technique: Small hand-labeled retrieval benchmark before optimizing
takeaways.what_they_do: When users complained search was bad, they hand-collected ~200 questions with the correct documents (including plausible-but-wrong ones), measured precision@10, then iterated against that benchmark.
takeaways.numbers: ~200 examples, <1 week; precision@10 went from ~60% to 90-95%

takeaways.what_they_do: Connecting the agent to the Vault prompts it to resolve an explicit time window (e.g., Oct 1-8) before searching, so it doesn't cite stale documents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the connection to the vault helps to prompt the agent that it should look for a specific period of time when answering my question
takeaways.numbers: 52 candidate docs vs 15; 7 sources used vs 1-2

takeaways.what_they_do: Production traces showed queries almost always carry a condition (date, source, asset); they switched from post-/pre-filtering to a vector DB with native filtering that searches only matching clusters.
takeaways.evidence_quote: almost always there was some condition, either as of a certain date or from a certain source or about a specific asset. And all of that requires advanced filtering
takeaways.numbers: fast like post-filtering with recall close to pre-filtering

takeaways.technique: Capture synthesis back into the corpus
takeaways.what_they_do: When a human and agent dig into a question together, the results are automatically written back into the Vault so the next turn starts from accumulated learning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the results of their collaboration are automatically captured back in the vault ... and puts it back in the corpus for the next turn

takeaways.technique: Design for human vs agent consumers separately
takeaways.what_they_do: They sized the platform for two very different readers: humans need precision/high signal-to-noise, agents tolerate lower precision but issue orders of magnitude more queries and read far faster.
takeaways.numbers: humans ~300 words/min, ~100 queries/hour, 300 users; agents 100+ queries/sec, swarms thousands/sec

takeaways.what_they_do: They moved agents from reactive Q&A to an 'investor workbench' where the agent continuously tracks topics and presents prioritized items needing attention.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent is always on tracking what's important to that investor and presenting them with the areas that are most in need of their attention
